questions.question_english: What is the full form of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, which govern the disciplinary mechanisms for Central Government servants?

Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules
Central Civil Services (Categorisation, Conduct and Appeal) Rules

questions.explanation_english: Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules The Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 provide the administrative framework governing disciplinary proceedings for Union Government servants. These statutory rules categorize government posts, delineate disciplinary authorities, establish procedure for minor and major penalties, and define appellate and revisionary mechanisms to ensure fair treatment, public accountability, and adherence to constitutional provisions across central government services.

questions.question_english: Under which Article of the Constitution of India were the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 promulgated by the President of India?

Article 311
Article 312
Article 315
questions.explanation_english: Article 309 Article 309 of the Constitution of India empowers the President or designated authorities to frame rules regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union. The Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 were formally promulgated under the proviso to this constitutional provision.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। संविधान का अनुच्छेद 309 राष्ट्रपति या उनके द्वारा अधिकृत प्राधिकारियों को संघ के कार्यों से संबंधित सार्वजनिक सेवाओं और पदों पर नियुक्त व्यक्तियों की भर्ती तथा सेवा-शर्तों को विनियमित करने वाले नियम बनाने की शक्ति देता है। CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 इसी अनुच्छेद के परंतुक के अंतर्गत बनाए गए थे।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)

questions.question_english: Which of the following fundamental principles of natural justice is heavily embedded in the procedures outlined within the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965?
options_english: Audi alteram partem
Ignorantia juris non excusat

questions.explanation_english: Audi alteram partem The principle of audi alteram partem, meaning hear the other side, is fundamental to natural justice and heavily embedded in disciplinary proceedings under central service rules. It mandates that no civil servant shall be condemned unheard, requiring prior notice, clear charge sheets, opportunities to submit written representations, and fair oral hearings before imposing any penalty.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। Audi alteram partem का अर्थ है कि निर्णय लेने से पहले दूसरे पक्ष को भी सुना जाए। यह प्राकृतिक न्याय का मूल सिद्धांत है और केंद्रीय सेवा नियमों के अंतर्गत अनुशासनात्मक कार्यवाही में महत्त्वपूर्ण है। इसके लिए कर्मचारी को पूर्व सूचना और स्पष्ट आरोप-पत्र देना, लिखित पक्ष प्रस्तुत करने का अवसर देना तथा दंड लगाने से पहले निष्पक्ष सुनवाई उपलब्ध कराना आवश्यक होता है।

questions.question_english: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the scope of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965.
options_english: They provide the framework for the classification of services.
They detail the procedures for imposing minor and major penalties.
They prescribe the substantive code of conduct for government employees.
They specify the appellate authorities for various disciplinary actions.
questions.explanation_english: They prescribe the substantive code of conduct for government employees. The Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 focus on classification of posts, procedural aspects of disciplinary actions, penalties, and appeals. Substantive rules governing employee conduct, duties, and restrictions are separately contained within the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964. Thus, conduct rules define misconduct, while classification and control rules prescribe procedures for taking action.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 पदों के वर्गीकरण, अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की प्रक्रिया, दंड और अपील से संबंधित हैं। सरकारी कर्मचारियों के आचरण, कर्तव्यों और प्रतिबंधों से जुड़े मूल नियम अलग से CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 में दिए गए हैं। इसलिए आचरण नियम यह बताते हैं कि कौन-सा व्यवहार अनुचित है, जबकि वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण और अपील नियम उसके विरुद्ध कार्रवाई की प्रक्रिया निर्धारित करते हैं।

CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 पदों के वर्गीकरण, अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की प्रक्रिया, दंड और अपील से संबंधित हैं

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 mandate that no government servant shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which they were appointed.
Reason (R): This constitutional safeguard is expressly derived from Article 311(1) of the Constitution of India.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A Article 311(1) of the Constitution provides a mandatory protection that no civil servant shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which they were appointed. The CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 incorporate this exact constitutional safeguard into statutory procedures, ensuring that appointing authorities or higher authorities hold exclusive jurisdiction for termination.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। संविधान का अनुच्छेद 311(1) यह सुरक्षा देता है कि किसी सिविल सेवक को उस प्राधिकारी से अधीनस्थ प्राधिकारी द्वारा बर्खास्त या सेवा से हटाया नहीं जाएगा जिसने उसकी नियुक्ति की थी। CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 इस संवैधानिक सुरक्षा को अनुशासनात्मक प्रक्रिया में समाहित करते हैं। इससे सेवा समाप्ति जैसे गंभीर निर्णयों पर सक्षम नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी या उससे उच्च प्राधिकारी का नियंत्रण सुनिश्चित होता है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)

questions.question_english: According to Rule 3 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, which of the following falls under the purview of these rules unless specifically excluded by the President?
options_english: A person in casual employment
A person employed as a temporary Group B officer
A person subject to discharge on less than one month’s notice
A person paid from contingencies
questions.explanation_english: A person employed as a temporary Group B officer Rule 3 specifies that the CCS (CCA) Rules apply to every government servant holding a civil post under the Union, including temporary posts, unless specifically excluded. Persons in casual employment, those paid from contingencies, or persons subject to discharge on short notice under contract terms are generally excluded, whereas temporary Group B civil posts fall under their scope.

questions.question_english: A newly recruited Post Graduate Teacher (PGT) in a GNCTD school is on a consolidated contractual salary for one year. The Head of School wishes to initiate formal disciplinary proceedings against the teacher under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 for insubordination. Which of the following is the most appropriate administrative evaluation of this decision?
options_english: The Head of School can proceed as the rules apply to all teaching staff.
The Head of School must upgrade the proceedings to a Rule 14 inquiry for contractual staff.
The Head of School cannot proceed as the rules do not apply to contractual employees.
The Head of School must transfer the matter to the Central Vigilance Commission.
questions.explanation_english: The Head of School cannot proceed as the rules do not apply to contractual employees. Contractual employees engaged on a consolidated salary are governed strictly by the terms and conditions specified in their individual employment contracts rather than statutory service rules. The CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 apply only to persons holding civil posts. Disciplinary action against contractual personnel must follow contractual termination clauses rather than standard statutory disciplinary inquiry procedures.

questions.question_english:

questions.question_english: A teacher in a government school is suspended pending an inquiry into financial embezzlement. questions.question_english: What is the fundamental difference between ‘Censure’ and a ‘Warning’ in the context of government service?

questions.question_english: Does the imposition of the minor penalty of ‘Censure’ operate as an absolute bar to the promotion of a Government servant?

questions.question_english: What is the practical implication of withholding an increment “without cumulative effect” for a period of one year?

III. संचयी प्रभाव के बिना वेतन-वृद्धि रोकना कर्मचारी के पेंशन लाभों को स्थायी रूप से प्रभावित करता है।
उपरोक्त में से कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल II और III
केवल I और III
I, II और III
questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the withholding of increment:
I. Withholding increment with cumulative effect is a major penalty.
II. During the period of withholding increment, the employee is still entitled to draw standard dearness allowance on the pre-penalty basic pay.
III. Withholding of increment without cumulative effect permanently affects the pension benefits of the employee. Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english: I and II only Withholding increments with cumulative effect permanently reduces future pay and is classified as a major penalty. During the penalty period, dearness allowance is calculated on the pre- penalty basic pay. Statement III is incorrect because withholding increments without cumulative effect restores pay and does not permanently affect pension calculation.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने से भविष्य का वेतन स्थायी रूप से कम हो सकता है, इसलिए इसे प्रमुख दंड माना जाता है। दंड अवधि में महँगाई भत्ते की गणना स्रोत में बताए अनुसार दंड से पहले के मूल वेतन पर होती है। कथन III गलत है, क्योंकि संचयी प्रभाव के बिना वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने पर वेतन बाद में सामान्य चरण पर बहाल हो जाता है और पेंशन पर स्थायी प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।

संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने से भविष्य का वेतन स्थायी रूप से कम हो सकता है, इसलिए इसे प्रमुख दंड माना जाता है

questions.question_hindi: एक TGT को 1 अप्रैल 2023 को ‘अगली वेतन-वृद्धि एक वर्ष के लिए संचयी प्रभाव के बिना रोकने’ का दंड दिया जाता है। उसकी वेतन-वृद्धि 1 जुलाई 2023 को देय थी। 1 जुलाई 2024 को उसके वेतन के साथ क्या होगा?
options_hindi: उसका वेतन उस स्तर पर बहाल हो जाएगा जहाँ वह 2023 के दंड के बिना पहुँचता।
उसे 2024 की केवल एक वेतन-वृद्धि मिलेगी, 2023 वाला स्तर बहाल नहीं होगा।
DPC द्वारा अभिलेख को स्वीकृति देने तक उसे 2023 वाला बिना-वृद्धि वेतन ही मिलता रहेगा।
उसे 2023 और 2024 दोनों वेतन-वृद्धियाँ पिछली तारीख से और पूरे बकाये सहित दी जाएँगी।
questions.question_english: A TGT is penalized with “withholding of next increment for a period of one year without cumulative effect” on 1st April 2023. His increment was due on 1st July 2023. What will happen to his pay on 1st July 2024?
options_english: His pay will be restored to the stage it would have reached without the 2023 penalty.
He will receive only the single increment due for 2024 without restoring the withheld 2023 stage.
He will continue to draw the un-incremented pay of 2023 until a DPC formally clears his record.
He will be granted both the 2023 and 2024 increments retroactively along with full back arrears.
questions.explanation_english: His pay will be restored to the stage it would have reached without the 2023 penalty. A penalty of withholding increment for one year without cumulative effect takes effect on the due date of increment. On 1st July 2024, when the penalty period of one year expires, the employee’s pay is restored to the exact stage it would have reached had no penalty been imposed.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। संचयी प्रभाव के बिना एक वर्ष के लिए वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने का दंड संबंधित वेतन-वृद्धि की देय तारीख पर प्रभावी होता है। 1 जुलाई 2024 को एक वर्ष की अवधि पूरी होने पर वेतन उस स्तर पर बहाल किया जाएगा जहाँ वह दंड नहीं लगाए जाने पर पहुँचता। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं है कि दो वेतन-वृद्धियाँ अलग से पिछली तारीख से दी जाएँगी।

संचयी प्रभाव के बिना एक वर्ष के लिए वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने का दंड संबंधित वेतन-वृद्धि की देय तारीख पर प्रभावी होता है

questions.question_english: The penalty of “withholding of promotion” under Rule 11 implies that:
options_english: The employee is declared permanently unfit for any future promotion across all cadre grades.
The employee is debarred from promotion for the period specified in the order.
The employee is demoted to a lower grade and kept there until they prove their overall fitness.
The employee’s total past service is completely forfeited for calculating promotional seniority.
questions.explanation_english: The employee is debarred from promotion for the period specified in the order. The statutory minor penalty of withholding of promotion under Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 debars the government employee from being promoted to a higher grade or post strictly during the period specified in the penalty order. It does not permanently bar future promotion nor forfeit past qualifying service.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। नियम 11 के अंतर्गत पदोन्नति रोकना एक वैधानिक लघु दंड है। इससे कर्मचारी दंड आदेश में निर्दिष्ट अवधि के दौरान उच्च ग्रेड या पद पर पदोन्नत नहीं हो सकता। यह भविष्य की सभी पदोन्नतियों पर स्थायी प्रतिबंध नहीं लगाता और न ही अपने-आप कर्मचारी की पूरी पूर्व सेवा जब्त करता है।

नियम 11 के अंतर्गत पदोन्नति रोकना एक वैधानिक लघु दंड है

questions.question_english: If an employee is penalized with “withholding of promotion” for two years, and their turn for regular promotion comes up during this penalty period, what action must the Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) take?

Consider the following situations:
I. Withholding of promotion as a specific penalty under Rule 11.
II. Non-promotion due to a government servant failing to pass a departmental examination prescribed for promotion. According to the explanation under Rule 11, does situation II amount to a penalty?
options_english: Yes, it is legally equivalent to the statutory minor penalty of withholding promotion.
Yes, it constitutes a statutory penalty provided the failure to pass is shown to be deliberate.
No, unless the competent authority officially issues a Censure for failing the exam.
No, it does not constitute a penalty under Rule 11.
questions.explanation_english: No, it does not constitute a penalty under Rule 11. According to the Explanation appended to Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, the non- promotion of a government servant due to failure to pass a mandatory departmental examination prescribed for promotion or eligibility does not amount to a statutory penalty within the meaning of disciplinary rules.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। नियम 11 के साथ दी गई व्याख्या के अनुसार, पदोन्नति या पात्रता के लिए निर्धारित अनिवार्य विभागीय परीक्षा पास न करने के कारण पदोन्नति न मिलना अपने-आप वैधानिक दंड नहीं है। यह स्थिति नियम 11 के अंतर्गत औपचारिक रूप से पदोन्नति रोकने के दंड से अलग है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (D)
नियम 11 के साथ दी गई व्याख्या के अनुसार, पदोन्नति या पात्रता के लिए निर्धारित अनिवार्य विभागीय परीक्षा पास न करने के कारण पदोन्नति न मिलना अपने-आप वैधानिक दंड नहीं है

questions.question_hindi: एक वरिष्ठ शिक्षक पर तीन वर्ष के लिए पदोन्नति रोकने का दंड लगा है। इसी अवधि में उसी वरिष्ठता सूची का एक कनिष्ठ शिक्षक पदोन्नत हो जाता है। वरिष्ठ शिक्षक शिकायत करता है कि कनिष्ठ को आगे बढ़ाना प्राकृतिक न्याय का उल्लंघन है। CCS (CCA) Rules के अनुसार निदेशालय को क्या उत्तर देना चाहिए?
options_hindi: शिकायत उचित नहीं है, क्योंकि कनिष्ठ की पदोन्नति वरिष्ठ पर लगे दंड का प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम है।
शिकायत सही है, क्योंकि दंडित वरिष्ठ के रहते कनिष्ठ को कभी पदोन्नत नहीं किया जा सकता।
निदेशालय को वरिष्ठ को उच्च पद पर पदोन्नत करना चाहिए, लेकिन संबंधित वेतनमान रोकना चाहिए।
निदेशालय को वरिष्ठ का दंड समाप्त होने तक कनिष्ठ की पदोन्नति रोकनी या उसे पदावनत करना चाहिए।
questions.question_english: A senior teacher is undergoing the penalty of withholding of promotion for three years. However, a junior teacher in the same seniority list is promoted during this period. The senior teacher files a grievance claiming his junior superseding him violates natural justice. How should the Directorate respond based on CCS (CCA) Rules?
options_english: The grievance is invalid, as promoting a junior is a direct outcome of the senior’s penalty.
The grievance is valid, because a junior employee can never be promoted while a senior is penalized.
The Directorate must promote the senior to the higher post but withhold the corresponding pay scale.
The Directorate must demote or withhold the junior’s promotion until the senior’s penalty ends.
questions.explanation_english: The grievance is invalid, as promoting a junior is a direct outcome of the senior’s penalty. When a senior employee is undergoing the penalty of withholding of promotion, they cannot be promoted during the penalty period. Eligible juniors can be promoted past them to fill available vacancies. Supersession resulting directly from an active penalty is legally valid and does not violate principles of natural justice.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। पदोन्नति रोकने का दंड लागू रहने के दौरान वरिष्ठ कर्मचारी को पदोन्नत नहीं किया जा सकता। रिक्त पद भरने के लिए पात्र कनिष्ठ कर्मचारियों को उससे आगे पदोन्नत किया जा सकता है। जब वरिष्ठ का पीछे रह जाना सक्रिय दंड का सीधा परिणाम हो, तो केवल इस आधार पर कनिष्ठ की पदोन्नति को प्राकृतिक न्याय का उल्लंघन नहीं माना जाता।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the minor penalty of withholding promotion:
I. It can only be imposed after holding a formal Rule 14 oral inquiry.
II. It requires the framing of a formal charge sheet under Rule 16.
III. The penalty order must clearly specify the period for which promotion is withheld.
IV. It permanently alters the seniority of the employee if a junior is promoted during the penalty period. Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I, II, and III
II, III, and IV
I, III, and IV
II and III only
questions.explanation_english: II, III, and IV Withholding promotion is a minor penalty requiring a Rule 16 charge sheet, explicit penalty duration, and alters relative seniority if a junior gets promoted during the penalty period. Statement I is incorrect because minor penalties do not inherently require a formal Rule 14 oral inquiry unless specifically ordered by the authority.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। पदोन्नति रोकना लघु दंड है, जिसके लिए नियम 16 के अंतर्गत ज्ञापन/आरोपों का विवरण, दंड की स्पष्ट अवधि और संबंधित वरिष्ठता प्रभावों का निर्धारण आवश्यक होता है। कथन I गलत है, क्योंकि लघु दंड के लिए नियम 14 की औपचारिक मौखिक जाँच अपने-आप अनिवार्य नहीं होती; यह आवश्यकता संबंधित नियमों और प्राधिकारी के निर्णय पर निर्भर करती है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (B)
पदोन्नति रोकना लघु दंड है, जिसके लिए नियम 16 के अंतर्गत ज्ञापन/आरोपों का विवरण, दंड की स्पष्ट अवधि और संबंधित वरिष्ठता प्रभावों का निर्धारण आवश्यक होता है

options_hindi: नियम 14 के तहत औपचारिक जाँच के बाद लगाया गया अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति का दंड
सेवा से बर्खास्तगी, जिसके कारण भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार के लिए वैधानिक अयोग्यता होती है

questions.question_english: Which of the following penalties is NOT categorized as a major penalty under Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965?
options_english: Compulsory retirement from service imposed as a statutory penalty following a formal inquiry under Rule 14.
Dismissal from service resulting in statutory disqualification for any future employment under Government.
Reduction to a lower pay stage for up to three years without cumulative effect.
Removal from service which terminates employment without barring future employment under Government.
questions.explanation_english: Reduction to a lower pay stage for up to three years without cumulative effect. Under Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, compulsory retirement, removal, dismissal, and reduction to a lower grade or post are major penalties. However, reduction to a lower stage in pay scale for a period not exceeding three years without cumulative effect is categorized as a minor penalty.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति, सेवा से हटाना, बर्खास्तगी और निचले पद या ग्रेड पर घटाना प्रमुख दंड हैं। लेकिन वेतनमान के निचले चरण पर तीन वर्ष से अधिक न होने वाली अवधि के लिए, संचयी प्रभाव के बिना वेतन घटाना नियम 11 के अंतर्गत लघु दंड माना जाता है। इसलिए विकल्प C अन्य प्रमुख दंडों से अलग है।

अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति, सेवा से हटाना, बर्खास्तगी और निचले पद या ग्रेड पर घटाना प्रमुख दंड हैं

कारण (R): प्रमुख दंड सरकारी कर्मचारी के करियर, आजीविका और पेंशन लाभों पर गंभीर प्रभाव डालते हैं, इसलिए संविधान के अनुच्छेद 311(2) के संरक्षण कठोरता से लागू होते हैं।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता
A सही है, लेकिन R गलत है

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The imposition of a major penalty under the CCS (CCA) Rules requires a detailed procedure including framing of formal charges and conducting an oral inquiry.
Reason (R): Major penalties severely impact the career, livelihood, and pensionary benefits of a Government servant, thereby attracting rigorous application of Article 311(2) protections.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A Major penalties significantly affect an employee’s career, pay, and retirement benefits. To protect civil servants from arbitrary action, Article 311(2) of the Constitution mandates that major penalties can only be imposed after holding a detailed formal inquiry, framing distinct charges, and giving a reasonable opportunity of defense.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। प्रमुख दंड कर्मचारी के करियर, वेतन और सेवानिवृत्ति लाभों पर गहरा प्रभाव डालते हैं। मनमानी कार्रवाई से रक्षा के लिए संविधान का अनुच्छेद 311(2) प्रमुख दंड लगाने से पहले औपचारिक जाँच, स्पष्ट आरोप और बचाव का उचित अवसर उपलब्ध कराने की अपेक्षा करता है। इस प्रकार कारण अभिकथन में वर्णित विस्तृत प्रक्रिया की आवश्यकता स्पष्ट करता है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)

questions.question_english: Reduction to a lower time-scale of pay, grade, post, or service is a major penalty. Which of the following conditions must be specified in the order imposing this penalty?

Whether on restoration, the period of reduction shall operate to postpone future increments
Whether the Government servant will regain his original seniority in the higher grade on restoration
All of the above

questions.question_hindi: ‘संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने’ के दंड का मूल अर्थ क्या है?

वेतन-वृद्धि रोकी जाएगी, जिससे भविष्य के वेतन और पेंशन की गणना पर स्थायी प्रभाव पड़ेगा।

questions.question_english: The penalty of “withholding of increments of pay with cumulative effect” fundamentally means that:
options_english: The employee will not get increments for the specified period, and all past service is forfeited for pay fixing.
The increment is withheld, permanently affecting all future pay and pension calculations.
The employee is permanently demoted to a lower pay scale without any provision for restoration of rank.
The amount of withheld increment is credited to the employee’s cumulative GPF account instead of being paid.
questions.explanation_english: The increment is withheld, permanently affecting all future pay and pension calculations. The penalty of withholding increments of pay with cumulative effect means that when the penalty period ends, the withheld increment is not restored to basic pay fixing. This creates a permanent reduction in basic pay, which continuously impacts all subsequent increments, allowances, and final pensionary entitlements of the employee.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने पर दंड की अवधि समाप्त होने के बाद रोकी गई वेतन-वृद्धि को मूल वेतन में बहाल नहीं किया जाता। इससे मूल वेतन स्थायी रूप से कम रहता है और आगे की वेतन-वृद्धियों, भत्तों तथा अंतिम पेंशन की गणना प्रभावित हो सकती है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (B)
संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने पर दंड की अवधि समाप्त होने के बाद रोकी गई वेतन-वृद्धि को मूल वेतन में बहाल नहीं किया जाता

questions.question_english: If a Government servant is reduced to a lower grade or post as a penalty, can they be reduced to a grade or post lower than the one to which they were initially directly recruited?
options_english: Yes, an employee can be reduced to any lower post if the proven misconduct is exceptionally grave.
Yes, provided the Disciplinary Authority obtains prior approval from the Union Public Service Commission.
No, an employee cannot be reduced below the grade to which they were initially recruited.
No, such a reduction is legally impermissible unless the employee expressly consents to it in writing.
questions.explanation_english: No, an employee cannot be reduced below the grade to which they were initially recruited. In disciplinary law under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, a government servant cannot be reduced to a post or grade lower than the one to which they were directly recruited into public service. Demoting an officer below their initial entry-level cadre post is legally impermissible and declared administrative action invalid.

questions.question_english: When a Government servant is penalized with reduction to a lower stage in the time-scale of pay, what is the maximum duration for which this major penalty can be imposed if it is with cumulative effect?

questions.question_english: An employee officiating in a higher post on an ad-hoc basis is reverted to their substantive lower post due to unsuitability for the higher post, completely unconnected with any disciplinary proceedings. options_english: No, administrative reversion from an officiating post to a substantive post is not a penalty.
Yes, because any administrative action that causes a direct financial loss of pay constitutes a penalty.

questions.explanation_english: No, administrative reversion from an officiating post to a substantive post is not a penalty. According to the Explanation under Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, reverting a government servant officiating in a higher post to their substantive lower post on administrative grounds or unsuitability does not constitute a statutory penalty. Penalty applies only when reduction in rank is ordered as formal punishment following disciplinary proceedings.

questions.question_english: Upon the expiry of the period of reduction to a lower grade (as a major penalty), if the order states that the employee will NOT regain his original seniority, what is the effect on the employee?
options_english: The employee must clear a fresh competitive recruitment examination to re-enter the higher grade.
The employee is restored to the higher grade but placed at the very bottom of the seniority list.
The employee is permanently barred from promotion and remains in the lower grade for rest of service.
Restoration occurs, but seniority is depressed by the period of reduction.
questions.explanation_english: Restoration occurs, but seniority is depressed by the period of reduction. When the period of reduction to a lower grade ends, the employee is restored to the higher grade. questions.question_english: When a Government servant is awarded the major penalty of compulsory retirement, what is the impact on their pension and gratuity under standard pension rules?

questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। स्रोत के अनुसार, दंड के रूप में अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति पर लागू पेंशन नियमों के तहत कर्मचारी को दो-तिहाई से लेकर पूरी प्रतिकर पेंशन/ग्रेच्युटी तक दिए जाने की संभावना हो सकती है। यह सामान्य अधिवर्षिता सेवानिवृत्ति के समान स्वतः पूर्ण लाभ मिलने की स्थिति नहीं है और न ही सभी लाभों का पूर्णतः समाप्त होना अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: A Principal with 22 years of qualifying service is found guilty of gross negligence leading to significant administrative failure. questions.question_english: Who is the lowest competent authority to impose the penalty of compulsory retirement on a Government servant?

Any Gazetted Officer serving as the administrative head of the department.
The designated Disciplinary Authority irrespective of appointing rank.
The Head of Office exercising administrative control over the employee.
questions.explanation_english: The Appointing Authority or an authority not subordinate to it Under Article 311(1) of the Constitution and Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, major penalties that terminate service, including compulsory retirement, removal, and dismissal, can only be imposed by the Appointing Authority or an authority higher than the appointing authority, never by a subordinate authority.

questions.question_english: Under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, the penalty of “Removal from service” fundamentally entails which of the following?
options_english: Termination of service with an absolute legal bar on any future employment under the Government.
Termination of service without barring future government employment.
Suspension from active government service for a mandatory minimum period of 10 years.
Forced submission of resignation without causing automatic forfeiture of past qualifying service.
questions.explanation_english: Termination of service without barring future government employment. Removal from service under Rule 11(viii) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 terminates the employment of a government servant. Unlike dismissal, removal does not disqualify the person from future employment under the Government, leaving them legally eligible to apply for public service positions in the future.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। नियम 11(viii) के अंतर्गत सेवा से हटाने का अर्थ सरकारी कर्मचारी की सेवा समाप्त करना है। बर्खास्तगी से अलग, सेवा से हटाने पर व्यक्ति भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार पाने के लिए स्वतः अयोग्य नहीं हो जाता। इसलिए वह भविष्य में सरकारी पदों के लिए आवेदन करने की कानूनी पात्रता बनाए रख सकता है।

questions.question_english: What is the usual effect of “Removal from service” on the pensionary benefits of a Government servant?

questions.question_english: A Head Clerk in a school manipulates accounts and embezzles Rs. 5 Lakhs. A departmental inquiry proves the charge beyond doubt. The Appointing Authority orders his “Dismissal from Service”. The clerk appeals, stating that since it was his first offence, he should have been allowed to resign. Is the Appointing Authority’s decision legally sound under the CCS (CCA) Rules?
options_english: Yes, embezzlement warrants dismissal, and resignation is not a right during proceedings.
No, first-time administrative offences cannot legally attract the extreme penalty of dismissal from service.
No, the appointing authority must offer the employee an option for voluntary retirement before dismissing him.
Yes, but the authority is mandated to refund the entire embezzled sum directly into the clerk’s GPF account.
questions.explanation_english: Yes, embezzlement warrants dismissal, and resignation is not a right during proceedings. Serious financial embezzlement warrants major penalties, including dismissal. Resignation is not a statutory right of an employee facing disciplinary proceedings, and the Appointing Authority is fully within its powers under Rule 11 and Article 311 to reject resignation requests and impose dismissal following proven inquiry findings.

questions.question_english: Mr. X was dismissed from the Department of Revenue for corruption. Five years later, he applies for a teaching position in the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, deliberately concealing his past employment and dismissal. He is selected, but during police verification, his past is revealed. What action is mandated under service rules?
options_english: He can be retained in service unconditionally because teaching is an entirely different profession.
He must face a fresh Rule 14 departmental inquiry specifically regarding his past corruption charge.
Services are terminated immediately, as dismissal disqualifies from future employment.
His salary will be attached to recover past administrative losses, but he may continue teaching.
questions.explanation_english: Services are terminated immediately, as dismissal disqualifies from future employment. Dismissal from service carries a mandatory statutory disqualification against securing future government employment. Securing subsequent public employment by suppressing material facts about a past dismissal renders the appointment illegal and void ab initio, resulting in immediate termination of services upon discovery during police verification or administrative checks.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। बर्खास्तगी भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार पाने के विरुद्ध वैधानिक अयोग्यता उत्पन्न करती है। पिछली बर्खास्तगी जैसे महत्त्वपूर्ण तथ्य छिपाकर दूसरी सरकारी नियुक्ति प्राप्त करना नियुक्ति को अवैध बना सकता है। पुलिस सत्यापन में तथ्य उजागर होने पर, स्रोत के अनुसार, सेवा समाप्त की जानी चाहिए; केवल पद का अलग होना इस अयोग्यता को समाप्त नहीं करता।

बर्खास्तगी भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार पाने के विरुद्ध वैधानिक अयोग्यता उत्पन्न करती है

questions.question_english: An Appointing Authority writes an order stating: “The services of Mr. Y are hereby terminated with immediate effect as he is removed from service. This order shall act as a bar on his future employment under the State.” What is the technical flaw in this order?
options_english: Termination and removal are legally mutually exclusive and cannot be used together in an order.
The order is legally flawed because it must specify the exact quantum of pension granted.
There is no legal flaw whatsoever, as the appointing authority holds full discretionary power.
Removal cannot bar future employment; only dismissal can.
questions.explanation_english: Removal cannot bar future employment; only dismissal can. The order contains a clear technical flaw because removal from service under Rule 11(viii) does not operate as a statutory disqualification for future employment under the Government. Only the penalty of dismissal from service under Rule 11(ix) carries the mandatory legal bar against securing future public employment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। नियम 11(viii) के अंतर्गत सेवा से हटाना भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार के लिए वैधानिक अयोग्यता नहीं बनाता। भविष्य की सरकारी नौकरी पर प्रतिबंध नियम 11(ix) के अंतर्गत बर्खास्तगी का प्रभाव है। इसलिए आदेश में सेवा से हटाने को भविष्य की नौकरी पर रोक से जोड़ना तकनीकी रूप से गलत है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (D)

questions.question_english: What is the fundamental procedural requirement before imposing a minor penalty under Rule 16?

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): In minor penalty proceedings, an oral inquiry is generally not mandatory.
Reason (R): The Disciplinary Authority has absolute discretion to deny an oral inquiry even if the charged officer specifically requests it and the authority believes it is necessary to establish the facts.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: A is true but R is false Assertion A is true because minor penalty procedures under Rule 16 generally do not require oral inquiries. II. किसी भी अवधि के लिए संचयी प्रभाव के साथ वेतन-वृद्धि रोकना।
III. वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने से देय पेंशन की राशि पर प्रतिकूल प्रभाव पड़ने की संभावना होना।
IV. प्रस्तावित दंड निंदा होना।
लघु दंड प्रस्तावित होने पर भी किन परिस्थितियों में नियम 14 के उपनियम (3) से (24) के अनुसार जाँच कराना अनिवार्य है?
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल II, III और IV
केवल I, III और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the following circumstances:
I. If the penalty proposed is withholding of increments of pay for a period exceeding 3 years.
II. If the penalty proposed is withholding of increments of pay with cumulative effect for any period.
III. If the penalty proposed is withholding of increments likely to affect adversely the amount of pension payable.
IV. If the penalty proposed is censure. Under which of the above circumstances is it mandatory to hold an inquiry in the manner laid down in sub-rules (3) to (24) of Rule 14 even when proposing a minor penalty?
options_english: I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV
questions.explanation_english:
I, II, and III only Under Rule 16(1-A), holding a Rule 14 oral inquiry is mandatory if withholding increment exceeds three years, is with cumulative effect, or adversely affects pension. Censure does not require a full inquiry under Rule 14, making
statement IV incorrect and making I, II, and III the correct combination.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। नियम 16(1-A) के अंतर्गत नियम 14 की मौखिक जाँच अनिवार्य है, यदि वेतन-वृद्धि तीन वर्ष से अधिक समय के लिए रोकी जा रही हो, संचयी प्रभाव के साथ रोकी जा रही हो या इससे पेंशन की राशि पर प्रतिकूल प्रभाव पड़ने की संभावना हो। निंदा के लिए अपने-आप ऐसी पूर्ण जाँच अनिवार्य नहीं है, इसलिए कथन IV सही संयोजन में शामिल नहीं है।

questions.question_english: Under Rule 14, no order imposing any of the major penalties shall be made except after:
options_english: A comprehensive criminal police investigation into the alleged misconduct is fully concluded.
The Central Administrative Tribunal examines the case records and issues prior legal clearance.
Holding an inquiry where the employee is informed of charges and heard.

Under Rule 14 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 and Article 311(2) of the Constitution, no major penalty can be imposed without holding a formal inquiry in which the employee is formally informed of specific charges, provided supporting evidence, and granted a fair opportunity to defend themselves.

questions.question_english: A Principal issues a major penalty charge sheet under Rule 14 to a laboratory assistant. The charge sheet merely states “You are charged with dereliction of duty on 12th May,” without attaching the statement of imputations, list of documents, or witnesses. Is this charge sheet procedurally valid?
options_english: Yes, procedural brevity is fully permissible if the alleged dereliction of duty is obvious from facts.
Yes, missing details and evidentiary lists can be validly provided later during the oral inquiry stage.
No, the charge sheet is invalid because it must be issued directly by the Directorate, not the Principal.
No, Rule 14 requires distinct charges, imputations, and lists of documents and witnesses.
questions.explanation_english: No, Rule 14 requires distinct charges, imputations, and lists of documents and witnesses. A charge sheet issued under Rule 14 must strictly contain distinct articles of charge, a detailed statement of imputations of misconduct, a list of documents relied upon, and a list of prosecution witnesses. Issuing a vague notice lacking these essential documents violates procedural requirements and renders the charge sheet invalid.

questions.question_english: In a Rule 14 inquiry, if the Government servant does not admit the charges or fails to submit a written statement of defense by the specified date, what is the mandatory next step for the Disciplinary Authority?

questions.explanation_english: To appoint an Inquiry Officer to inquire into the charges. questions.question_english: In which of the following exceptional cases can the procedure of holding an inquiry under Rule 14 be dispensed with, as provided under Rule 19?
options_english: Where any major penalty is imposed on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge.
Where the Disciplinary Authority is satisfied for reasons to be recorded that it is not reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry.
Where the President is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State, it is not expedient to hold any inquiry.

questions.question_hindi:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं: एक अभिकथन (A) है और दूसरा कारण (R) है।
अभिकथन (A): आरोप-पत्र में लिखे आरोपों से यह संकेत नहीं मिलना चाहिए कि अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी ने पहले ही कर्मचारी को दोषी मान लिया है।
कारण (R): ‘आप दोषी हैं’ जैसी निर्णायक भाषा के बजाय ‘यह आरोप है कि…’ जैसी भाषा प्रयोग करना आवश्यक है, क्योंकि निर्णायक भाषा पूर्वाग्रह दर्शाती है और निष्पक्ष जाँच के सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करती है।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता
A सही है, लेकिन R गलत है
A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है
questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The charges framed in a charge sheet must not indicate that the Disciplinary Authority has already made up its mind about the guilt of the employee.
Reason (R): Using definitive language like “You are guilty of...” instead of “It is alleged that you...” violates the principle of an unbiased inquiry and indicates a pre-judged mindset.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A The language of a charge sheet must remain tentative and conditional, using phrasing like “it is alleged that.” Using conclusive expressions such as “you are guilty of” indicates a pre-judged mindset by the authority, violating the principle of an unbiased inquiry and breaching mandatory principles of natural justice.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। आरोप-पत्र की भाषा आरोपात्मक और अस्थायी होनी चाहिए, जैसे ‘यह आरोप है कि…’। ‘आप दोषी हैं’ जैसी निर्णायक भाषा यह संकेत दे सकती है कि प्राधिकारी ने जाँच से पहले ही निष्कर्ष निकाल लिया है। इससे निष्पक्ष जाँच और प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांत प्रभावित होते हैं। इसलिए दोनों कथन सही हैं और कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)
आरोप-पत्र की भाषा आरोपात्मक और अस्थायी होनी चाहिए, जैसे ‘यह आरोप है कि…’

questions.question_english: How must a charge sheet under Rule 14 be delivered to the charged Government servant to ensure procedural validity?
options_english: It must be officially published in a leading local newspaper having wide circulation.
It must be read out verbally in person to the employee in the presence of two witnesses.
It must be uploaded on the department’s public website and notified on the bulletin board.
It must be served in person or sent by registered post with acknowledgment due.
questions.explanation_english: It must be served in person or sent by registered post with acknowledgment due. To satisfy statutory procedural validity and natural justice, a Rule 14 charge sheet must be officially served directly on the government servant in person against written acknowledgment or dispatched to their last known address by registered post with acknowledgment due, ensuring verifiable legal proof of delivery.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। प्राकृतिक न्याय और प्रक्रिया की वैधता के लिए आरोप-पत्र कर्मचारी को व्यक्तिगत रूप से देकर लिखित पावती ली जा सकती है या अंतिम ज्ञात पते पर पावती सहित पंजीकृत डाक से भेजा जा सकता है। इससे यह सत्यापित किया जा सकता है कि आरोप-पत्र कर्मचारी तक पहुँचाया गया और उसे अपना बचाव करने का अवसर मिला।

questions.question_english: Who has the statutory authority to appoint an Inquiring Authority (Inquiry Officer) under Rule 14(2) of the CCS (CCA) Rules?

questions.explanation_english: The Disciplinary Authority Under Rule 14(2) and Rule 14(5) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, the Disciplinary Authority holds the exclusive statutory authority to appoint an Inquiring Authority (Inquiry Officer) to conduct a formal oral inquiry into articles of charge that are not admitted by the charged government servant.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। नियम 14(2) और 14(5) के अंतर्गत जाँच अधिकारी नियुक्त करने का अधिकार अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी के पास होता है। जाँच अधिकारी उन आरोपों की औपचारिक जाँच करता है जिन्हें कर्मचारी ने स्वीकार नहीं किया है। प्रस्तुतकर्ता अधिकारी साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत करता है, लेकिन उसे जाँच अधिकारी नियुक्त करने का अधिकार नहीं है।

questions.question_english: Which of the following best describes the role of an Inquiry Officer (IO) during disciplinary proceedings?
options_english: To act as an active prosecutor presenting arguments solely on behalf of the Disciplinary Authority.
An impartial fact-finder who evaluates evidence to determine if charges are proved.
To act as an independent defense counsel safeguarding the procedural rights of the charged officer.
To decide the quantum of punishment and directly impose the final penalty on the charged officer.
questions.explanation_english: An impartial fact-finder who evaluates evidence to determine if charges are proved. The Inquiry Officer acts as an independent quasi-judicial fact-finder. Their role is to record evidence objectively, conduct inquiry proceedings fairly, evaluate prosecution and defense arguments, and record logical findings on whether each article of charge is proved or not, without acting as a prosecutor or punishment authority.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। जाँच अधिकारी निष्पक्ष, अर्ध-न्यायिक तथ्य-निर्धारक की भूमिका निभाता है। वह साक्ष्य दर्ज करता है, जाँच की निष्पक्ष कार्यवाही सुनिश्चित करता है और अभियोजन तथा बचाव के साक्ष्यों का मूल्यांकन करके प्रत्येक आरोप के सिद्ध होने या न होने पर कारणयुक्त निष्कर्ष देता है। वह न तो अभियोजक होता है और न ही अंतिम दंड लगाने वाला प्राधिकारी।

options_hindi: हाँ, क्योंकि तथ्यात्मक पृष्ठभूमि की जानकारी जाँच को अधिक कुशल बनाती है।
हाँ, यदि प्रारंभिक जाँच अधिकारी का पद आरोपित कर्मचारी से वरिष्ठ हो।
नहीं, इससे पहले से बने विचारों के कारण पूर्वाग्रह उत्पन्न होता है और प्राकृतिक न्याय प्रभावित होता है।
नहीं, नियमों के अनुसार केवल सेवानिवृत्त न्यायिक अधिकारी ही जाँच अधिकारी हो सकता है।
questions.question_english: Can the officer who conducted the preliminary investigation (fact-finding inquiry) be appointed as the Inquiry Officer for the regular departmental inquiry in the same case?
options_english: Yes, because having prior knowledge of the factual background ensures a more efficient inquiry.
Yes, provided the preliminary investigating officer holds a rank senior to the charged officer.
No, doing so violates natural justice by creating bias from prior investigation.
No, service rules strictly require that only a retired judicial officer can serve as Inquiry Officer.
questions.explanation_english: No, doing so violates natural justice by creating bias from prior investigation. Appointing the officer who conducted the preliminary fact-finding investigation as the Inquiry Officer violates natural justice principles. Having formed prior opinions, the preliminary investigating officer carries inherent bias, rendering them legally ineligible to conduct an impartial regular departmental inquiry into the same charges against the employee.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। प्रारंभिक तथ्य-जाँच कर चुके अधिकारी ने मामले के बारे में पहले ही विचार बना लिया हो सकता है। उसी अधिकारी को नियमित जाँच सौंपने से निष्पक्षता पर संदेह उत्पन्न होता है और प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांत प्रभावित हो सकते हैं। इसलिए स्रोत के अनुसार, ऐसे अधिकारी को उसी मामले में नियमित विभागीय जाँच का जाँच अधिकारी नियुक्त करना उचित नहीं है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (C)

questions.question_english: What does the final report of the Inquiry Officer contain?
options_english: Specific administrative recommendations on the exact quantum of penalty to be imposed on the officer.
A final and legally binding judgment that cannot be altered or set aside by the Disciplinary Authority.
The complete verified service book and entire administrative career dossier of the charged officer.
Findings on each article of charge detailing if proved or not, with reasons.
questions.explanation_english: Findings on each article of charge detailing if proved or not, with reasons. The Inquiry Officer’s final report must contain a detailed assessment of oral and documentary evidence presented during proceedings and record explicit findings on each article of charge, stating whether it is proved, not proved, or partially proved, supported by clear, logical reasoning based on evidence.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। जाँच अधिकारी की अंतिम रिपोर्ट में कार्यवाही के दौरान प्रस्तुत मौखिक और दस्तावेजी साक्ष्यों का मूल्यांकन होना चाहिए। प्रत्येक आरोप के संबंध में स्पष्ट निष्कर्ष दर्ज किया जाता है कि वह सिद्ध, असिद्ध या आंशिक रूप से सिद्ध है, और निष्कर्षों के समर्थन में कारण दिए जाते हैं। अंतिम दंड निर्धारित करना अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी का काम है।

questions.question_english: What is the role of a Presenting Officer (PO) in a regular departmental inquiry?

To present the case and evidence supporting charges for the Disciplinary Authority.
To assist and represent the charged officer in conducting their defense during proceedings.
To formally serve administrative summons and notices to all prosecution and defense witnesses.
questions.explanation_english: To present the case and evidence supporting charges for the Disciplinary Authority. The Presenting Officer (PO) is appointed to represent the Disciplinary Authority during a Rule 14 inquiry. questions.question_english: During an inquiry, a prosecution witness turns hostile and gives testimony favoring the charged officer. What action can the Presenting Officer (PO) take?

The PO can immediately initiate criminal proceedings to arrest the witness for perjury.
The PO is legally required to immediately withdraw the charge sheet against the employee.
The PO can request the IO’s permission to cross-examine their own witness.
questions.explanation_english: The PO can request the IO’s permission to cross-examine their own witness. When a prosecution witness gives evidence contradictory to earlier statements or favors the defense, the witness is treated as hostile. In such situations, the Presenting Officer can request permission from the Inquiry Officer to cross- examine their own witness to test credibility and bring out true facts.

questions.question_english: In the context of disciplinary proceedings, what is the purpose of the mandatory communication (often referred to as a show cause notice/ opportunity to represent) given to the charged officer after the Inquiry Officer submits their report?

questions.question_english: Previously, a “second show cause notice” on the exact quantum of proposed penalty was required. This requirement was dispensed with following which Constitutional Amendment?
options_english: 42nd Amendment
44th Amendment
73rd Amendment
86th Amendment
questions.explanation_english: 42nd Amendment Prior to 1976, a second show-cause notice proposing the specific quantum of penalty was mandatory. The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 amended Article 311(2), dispensing with the requirement of giving a second opportunity to represent against the proposed penalty, requiring representation only on the inquiry report findings.

questions.question_english: If the Disciplinary Authority disagrees with the findings of the Inquiry Officer (e.g., the IO finds a charge ‘not proved’, but the DA believes evidence shows it is ‘proved’), what must the Disciplinary Authority do before imposing a penalty?

Order a completely fresh inquiry to be conducted by a newly appointed independent Inquiry Officer.
Forward tentative reasons for disagreement with the IO report for representation.
Refer the disciplinary file directly to the relevant High Court for binding judicial adjudication.
questions.explanation_english: Forward tentative reasons for disagreement with the IO report for representation. If the Disciplinary Authority disagrees with the Inquiry Officer’s findings on any charge, it must record its tentative reasons for disagreement. It must forward these disagreement notes along with the IO report to the charged officer, inviting their written representation before taking a final decision on the charges.

questions.question_hindi:

I. जाँच अधिकारी की रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होती है, जिसमें आरोप सिद्ध बताए गए हैं।

III. रिपोर्ट की प्रति सेवा-पुस्तिका में रख दी जाती है।
वर्तमान नियमों के अंतर्गत इस क्रम में कानूनी रूप से क्या गलत है?
options_hindi: अंतिम आदेश से पहले कर्मचारी को प्रतिनिधित्व के लिए जाँच रिपोर्ट उपलब्ध नहीं कराई गई।
अंतिम आदेश से पहले अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी को CAT की अनिवार्य स्वीकृति लेनी चाहिए थी।
सेवा से हटाने से पहले औपचारिक प्रशासनिक चेतावनी देना आवश्यक था।
प्रक्रिया पूरी तरह सही है, क्योंकि अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी को पूर्ण अधिकार है।
questions.question_english:
Consider the following sequence of actions by a Disciplinary Authority:
I. Receiving the IO report stating charges are proved.
II. Directly passing an order for removal from service without sharing the report.
III. Filing a copy of the report in the service book. What is legally incorrect about this sequence under current rules?
options_english: Failing to furnish the IO report to the officer for representation prior to final order.
The Disciplinary Authority is required to seek mandatory approval from CAT before passing the final order.
The Disciplinary Authority was legally required to issue a formal administrative warning prior to removal.
The administrative procedure followed is entirely correct, as the Disciplinary Authority holds absolute power.
questions.explanation_english: Failing to furnish the IO report to the officer for representation prior to final order. Passing a major penalty order without serving the Inquiry Officer’s report on the charged officer for representation violates natural justice and principles established in landmark judicial decisions. The report must be furnished to enable representation before the Disciplinary Authority decides on guilt or penalty.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। जाँच अधिकारी की रिपोर्ट कर्मचारी को प्रतिनिधित्व के लिए दिए बिना प्रमुख दंड का आदेश पारित करना प्राकृतिक न्याय का उल्लंघन है। कर्मचारी को रिपोर्ट की प्रति मिलनी चाहिए, ताकि वह निष्कर्षों के विरुद्ध अपना पक्ष रख सके। रिपोर्ट को बाद में सेवा-पुस्तिका में रख देना, पहले अवसर न देने की कमी को दूर नहीं करता।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)
जाँच अधिकारी की रिपोर्ट कर्मचारी को प्रतिनिधित्व के लिए दिए बिना प्रमुख दंड का आदेश पारित करना प्राकृतिक न्याय का उल्लंघन है

questions.question_english: Under Rule 22, no appeal lies against which of the following orders?
options_english: An order of suspension made under Rule 10
Any order made by the President
An order imposing any of the penalties specified in Rule 11
An order enhancing a penalty
questions.explanation_english: Any order made by the President Under Rule 22 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, no departmental appeal lies against any order made by the President of India. Since the President is the highest executive administrative authority, orders passed by the President are exempt from departmental appeals, though revision or review mechanisms may apply.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। नियम 22 के अनुसार, भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा पारित आदेश के विरुद्ध विभागीय अपील नहीं होती। राष्ट्रपति सर्वोच्च कार्यकारी प्राधिकारी हैं, इसलिए उनके आदेशों के विरुद्ध विभागीय अपील की सामान्य व्यवस्था लागू नहीं होती; हालांकि नियमों के अंतर्गत पुनरीक्षण या समीक्षा जैसी व्यवस्थाएँ अलग से लागू हो सकती हैं।

questions.question_english: An order is passed by a Disciplinary Authority imposing the penalty of withholding one increment. The aggrieved employee wishes to appeal. To whom should the appeal generally be directed?
options_english: The Central Vigilance Commission acting as the statutory appellate body.
The President of India exercising supreme executive administrative power.
The authority immediately superior to the Disciplinary Authority.
The Head of Office exercising direct administrative control in all cases.
questions.explanation_english: The authority immediately superior to the Disciplinary Authority. Under Rule 24 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, a government servant may prefer an appeal against an order imposing a penalty to the Appellate Authority. The designated Appellate Authority is generally the authority immediately superior to the Disciplinary Authority that passed the original penalty order.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। सामान्यतः अपील संबंधित नियमों और पद के लिए निर्धारित अपीलीय प्राधिकारी को की जाती है। वेतन-वृद्धि रोकने का दंड लगाने वाले अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी से तत्काल वरिष्ठ प्राधिकारी आम तौर पर अपील का उचित स्तर होगा, बशर्ते अनुसूची में अलग सक्षम अपीलीय प्राधिकारी निर्दिष्ट न हो। केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयोग या राष्ट्रपति प्रत्येक ऐसे मामले के सामान्य अपीलीय प्राधिकारी नहीं हैं।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following orders:
I. An order passed by an Inquiring Authority in the course of an inquiry under Rule 14.
II. An order placing a Government servant under suspension.

questions.explanation_english: I and III only Under Rule 22, no appeal lies against interlocutory orders passed by an Inquiry Officer during inquiry proceedings (I) or against any order passed by the President (III). questions.question_english: A Government servant files an appeal against a penalty order. While the appeal is pending with the Appellate Authority, can the Revising Authority take up the case for revision?

questions.question_english: If an Appellate Authority has already passed an order on an appeal, can a revision petition be entertained against that appellate order?

questions.question_english: What is the explicit statutory ground on which a ‘Review’ under Rule 29-A can be exercised by the President?
options_english: If the charged employee formally tenders a unconditional written public apology to the authority.

questions.explanation_english: Discovery of new material evidence that was unavailable earlier and alters the case. questions.question_hindi:

I. पुनरीक्षण कई निर्दिष्ट प्राधिकारी कर सकते हैं, जबकि समीक्षा केवल राष्ट्रपति कर सकते हैं।
II. पुनरीक्षण के लिए नए महत्त्वपूर्ण साक्ष्य का मिलना आवश्यक है।
III. समीक्षा और पुनरीक्षण, दोनों से दंड आदेश को रद्द या संशोधित किया जा सकता है।
उपरोक्त में से कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल I और III
केवल II और III
I, II और III
questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding Review and Revision:
I. Revision can be undertaken by multiple designated authorities (like the President, CAG, Secretary, etc.), while Review can only be undertaken by the President.
II. Revision requires the discovery of new material evidence.
III. Both Review and Revision can result in the setting aside or modification of a penalty. Which of the above statements are correct?

I and III only
II and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english: I and III only Revision can be exercised by multiple designated authorities, whereas Review under Rule 29-A is exclusive to the President. Statement II is incorrect because Review requires discovery of new material evidence, whereas Revision under Rule 29 does not require new evidence. Both mechanisms can modify or set aside penalty orders.

questions.question_hindi: एक कर्मचारी को सेवा से बर्खास्त कर दिया गया और उसकी अपील तथा पुनरीक्षण याचिकाएँ खारिज हो गईं। तीन वर्ष बाद ऐसा निर्णायक दस्तावेज मिलता है जो साबित करता है कि धोखाधड़ी किसी और ने की थी और कर्मचारी को झूठा फँसाया गया था। CCS (CCA) Rules के अंतर्गत उसे कौन-सी प्रक्रिया अपनानी चाहिए?
options_hindi: नामित अपीलीय प्राधिकारी के समक्ष दूसरी प्रशासनिक अपील
पुनरीक्षण प्राधिकारी के समक्ष दूसरी वैधानिक पुनरीक्षण याचिका
राष्ट्रपति के समक्ष नियम 29-A के अंतर्गत समीक्षा याचिका

questions.question_english: An employee was dismissed from service, and his appeal and revision petitions were rejected. Three years later, a crucial document is discovered that conclusively proves someone else committed the fraud and the employee was framed. Which procedural mechanism under CCS (CCA) Rules should the employee invoke?
options_english: A second administrative appeal to the designated appellate authority.
A second statutory revision petition to the revising authority.
A Review petition under Rule 29-A to the President.
A fresh regular departmental inquiry under Rule 14 provisions.
questions.explanation_english: A Review petition under Rule 29-A to the President. When appeals and revision petitions have already been exhausted and new material evidence proving innocence is discovered later, the appropriate procedural mechanism under the CCS (CCA) Rules is filing a Review petition under Rule 29-A addressed to the President of India based on newly discovered facts.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। जब अपील और पुनरीक्षण के उपाय समाप्त हो चुके हों, लेकिन बाद में निर्दोषता सिद्ध करने वाला नया महत्त्वपूर्ण साक्ष्य मिल जाए, तो स्रोत के अनुसार उचित प्रक्रिया नियम 29-A के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति के समक्ष समीक्षा याचिका दायर करना है। समीक्षा नई जानकारी पर आधारित होती है जो पहले उपलब्ध नहीं थी और मामले के परिणाम को बदल सकती है।

questions.question_english: Under Rule 26 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, what is the standard time limit for a Government servant to submit an appeal against an order imposing a penalty?

Within 45 days from delivery of the order to the appellant.
Within 60 days calculated directly from the date of issuance of the administrative order.
Within 90 days calculated from the official date of dispatch of the penalty order copy.
questions.explanation_english: Within 45 days from delivery of the order to the appellant. Under Rule 26 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, an appeal must be preferred within a limitation period of 45 days. This period is calculated from the date on which a copy of the order appealed against is delivered or served upon the aggrieved government servant.

questions.question_english: If an appeal is filed after the expiry of the 45-day period, what action can the Appellate Authority take?

questions.question_english: According to Rule 29, what is the time limit for an authority (other than the President) to initiate suo motu revision of a disciplinary order?

questions.explanation_english: 6 months from the date of the order to be revised. Under Rule 29(1) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, an authority other than the President (such as Head of Department or Appellate Authority) can exercise powers of suo motu revision within a statutory time limit of six months from the date of the order proposed to be revised.

questions.question_english: How should an appellant submit their appeal under the rules?
options_english: To the Appellate Authority, copying the authority that passed the order.
Directly to the Appellate Authority while withholding intimation to the Disciplinary Authority.

questions.explanation_english: To the Appellate Authority, copying the authority that passed the order. questions.question_english: In the context of a departmental inquiry under Rule 14, what is the meaning of “ex-parte” proceedings?

questions.question_english: If an Inquiry Officer decides to proceed ex-parte because the charged officer refuses to attend the hearings, what is the obligation of the Presenting Officer (PO)?

The PO must request the local police authority to arrest the charged officer for non-attendance.
The PO must still present evidence to prove the charges before the IO.

questions.explanation_english: The PO must still present evidence to prove the charges before the IO. Even in ex-parte proceedings under Rule 14(20), charges are not automatically treated as proved. The Presenting Officer is still legally required to introduce documentary evidence and examine prosecution witnesses to establish the charges, ensuring the Inquiry Officer evaluates evidence before coming to findings.

questions.question_english: A charged officer refuses to submit their written statement of defense and ignores all summons to attend the inquiry. The Inquiry Officer proceeds ex-parte and concludes the inquiry. Which of the following statements is true regarding this scenario?
options_english: The ex-parte inquiry inherently violates natural justice because the employee was not personally heard.
The IO is legally required to wait indefinitely until the charged officer chooses to appear in person.
The Disciplinary Authority cannot legally impose any major penalty based on an ex- parte inquiry report.
The ex-parte inquiry is valid as reasonable opportunity was provided but not availed.
questions.explanation_english: The ex-parte inquiry is valid as reasonable opportunity was provided but not availed. Natural justice requires providing a reasonable opportunity of defense, not forcing an employee to participate. If notice was duly served and the employee deliberately refrains from appearing without sufficient cause, conducting ex-parte proceedings under Rule 14(20) is procedurally valid and fully legally sustainable.

questions.question_english: During a Rule 14 inquiry, who acts as the Defense Assistant (often referred to as Assisting Government Servant) for the charged officer?

Any practicing advocate registered with the High Court Bar Association.

questions.question_english: Under what condition is a charged officer strictly permitted to engage a legal practitioner as their Defense Assistant during a departmental inquiry?

questions.explanation_english: The Inquiry Officer The daily order sheet is a statutory procedural record of day-to-day proceedings maintained by the Inquiry Officer during a departmental inquiry under Rule 14. It records attendance, rulings, adjournment reasons, and witness examinations, signed by the IO, PO, charged officer, and defense assistant.

questions.question_hindi:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं: एक अभिकथन (A) है और दूसरा कारण (R)।
अभिकथन (A): विभागीय जाँच में प्रमाण का मानक “संभावनाओं की प्रबलता” (preponderance of probabilities) है, न कि “उचित संदेह से परे प्रमाण” (proof beyond reasonable doubt)।
कारण (R): विभागीय कार्यवाही आपराधिक मुकदमा नहीं है; इसका उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक सेवा में अनुशासन और शुचिता बनाए रखना है।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
A सत्य है, लेकिन R असत्य है।
A असत्य है, लेकिन R सत्य है।
questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): In a departmental inquiry, the standard of proof required is “preponderance of probabilities” and not “proof beyond reasonable doubt.”
Reason (R): Departmental proceedings are not criminal trials; they are meant to maintain discipline and purity in public service.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A Departmental inquiries are administrative proceedings aimed at evaluating administrative misconduct and maintaining purity of public administration. Unlike criminal trials requiring proof beyond reasonable doubt, departmental inquiries operate under the standard of preponderance of probabilities to determine whether allegations are established by evidence.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। विभागीय जाँच का उद्देश्य सेवा-संबंधी कदाचार का प्रशासनिक मूल्यांकन और सार्वजनिक प्रशासन में अनुशासन बनाए रखना है। आपराधिक मुकदमों में लागू “उचित संदेह से परे” प्रमाण के कठोर मानक के बजाय विभागीय जाँच सामान्यतः “संभावनाओं की प्रबलता” के मानक पर आधारित होती है। इसलिए दोनों कथन सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की व्याख्या करता है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)
विभागीय जाँच का उद्देश्य सेवा-संबंधी कदाचार का प्रशासनिक मूल्यांकन और सार्वजनिक प्रशासन में अनुशासन बनाए रखना है

questions.question_hindi: यदि अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी नियम 14 के अंतर्गत प्रमुख दंड की कार्यवाही शुरू करता है, लेकिन जाँच रिपोर्ट पढ़ने के बाद यह तय करता है कि केवल लघु दंड उचित है, तो सही प्रक्रियात्मक कदम क्या है?

दंड घटाने से पहले केंद्रीय प्रशासनिक अधिकरण से अनुमति लेना अनिवार्य है।
लघु दंड लगाने से पहले आरोपित अधिकारी की स्पष्ट लिखित सहमति लेना अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: If a Disciplinary Authority initiates proceedings for a major penalty under Rule 14, but after reading the Inquiry Report, decides that only a minor penalty is warranted, what is the correct procedural action?
options_english: The DA must completely drop the major charge sheet and initiate fresh proceedings under Rule 16 rules.
The DA must refer the complete file to CAT to obtain prior permission to downgrade the penalty.
The DA must seek explicit written consent from the charged officer prior to imposing a minor penalty.
The DA can impose a minor penalty based on Rule 14 proceedings without a fresh charge sheet.
questions.explanation_english: The DA can impose a minor penalty based on Rule 14 proceedings without a fresh charge sheet. Under Rule 15 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, if major penalty proceedings were conducted under Rule 14, but after considering the inquiry report the Disciplinary Authority concludes that only a minor penalty is warranted, it can directly impose a minor penalty without initiating fresh Rule 16 proceedings.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। नियम 15 के अनुसार, यदि नियम 14 के तहत प्रमुख दंड की जाँच की गई हो और जाँच रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के बाद अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी यह निष्कर्ष निकाले कि लघु दंड पर्याप्त है, तो वह उसी कार्यवाही के आधार पर लघु दंड लगा सकता है। केवल दंड की श्रेणी बदलने के कारण नई आरोप-पत्र प्रक्रिया शुरू करना आवश्यक नहीं है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (D)

questions.question_hindi:
नियम 14 और नियम 16 के बीच प्रक्रियात्मक अंतरों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. नियम 14 में आरोपों के अनुच्छेद और आरोपों के विवरण की आवश्यकता होती है; नियम 16 में सामान्यतः आरोपों के विवरण का प्रावधान होता है।
II. नियम 14 में मौखिक जाँच की व्यवस्था है; नियम 16 में सामान्यतः मौखिक जाँच नहीं होती।
III. नियम 14 में गवाहों से जिरह का अधिकार होता है, जबकि नियम 16 में सामान्यतः यह लागू नहीं होता।
IV. पदावनति (reduction in rank) का दंड नियम 16 के तहत दिया जा सकता है।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल II, III और IV
केवल I, III और IV
I, II, III और IV
questions.question_english:
Consider the following procedural differences between Rule 14 and Rule 16:
I. Rule 14 always requires articles of charge and statement of imputations; Rule 16 only requires a statement of imputations.
II. Rule 14 mandates an oral inquiry; Rule 16 normally dispenses with an oral inquiry.
III. Cross-examination of witnesses is a right in Rule 14 but not normally applicable in Rule 16.
IV. The penalty of reduction in rank can be given under Rule 16.
Which statements are correct?
options_english: I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV
questions.explanation_english:
I, II, and III only Rule 14 involves detailed charge sheets, oral inquiries, and cross-examination, whereas Rule 16 normally dispenses with oral inquiries.
Statement IV is incorrect because reduction in rank is a major penalty which can never be imposed under minor penalty procedures under Rule 16 without following Rule 14 procedures.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। नियम 14 में विस्तृत आरोप-पत्र, मौखिक जाँच तथा गवाहों से जिरह जैसी प्रक्रियाएँ शामिल होती हैं। नियम 16 की लघु दंड प्रक्रिया में सामान्यतः मौखिक जाँच नहीं होती, हालांकि नियमानुसार जाँच आवश्यक समझे जाने पर संबंधित प्रक्रिया अपनाई जाती है। कथन IV गलत है, क्योंकि पदावनति प्रमुख दंड है और इसे केवल नियम 16 की प्रक्रिया के आधार पर नहीं लगाया जा सकता।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)
नियम 14 में विस्तृत आरोप-पत्र, मौखिक जाँच तथा गवाहों से जिरह जैसी प्रक्रियाएँ शामिल होती हैं

questions.question_english: Under Rule 16, if the Disciplinary Authority is of the opinion that an inquiry is necessary before imposing a minor penalty, what procedure must be followed?
options_english: It must follow the inquiry procedure prescribed under Rule 14.
It must request the local police department to conduct a preliminary investigation.
It must hold an informal administrative meeting with the employee to discuss charges.
It must constitute a formal committee comprising three senior gazetted officers.
questions.explanation_english: It must follow the inquiry procedure prescribed under Rule 14. Under Rule 16(1)(b) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, if the Disciplinary Authority decides that an oral inquiry is necessary in a minor penalty case, it must conduct the inquiry in the exact manner prescribed in sub-rules (3) to (24) of Rule 14 for major penalties.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। नियम 16(1)(b) के अनुसार, यदि अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी लघु दंड के मामले में जाँच करना आवश्यक समझता है, तो नियम 14 के उपनियम (3) से (24) में निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के अनुसार जाँच की जाती है। इसलिए केवल अनौपचारिक बैठक या पुलिस जाँच, नियमों में बताई गई विभागीय जाँच का विकल्प नहीं है।
key_facts: उत्तर-कुंजी: (A)
नियम 16(1)(b) के अनुसार, यदि अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी लघु दंड के मामले में जाँच करना आवश्यक समझता है, तो नियम 14 के उपनियम (3) से (24) में निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के अनुसार जाँच की जाती है

अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति (Compulsory Retirement)

आर्थिक हानि की वसूली
questions.question_english: Which of the following penalties can NEVER be imposed if proceedings were conducted purely under Rule 16 (without invoking the inquiry provisions of Rule 14)?
options_english: Censure
Compulsory Retirement
Withholding of increment for one year
Recovery of pecuniary loss
questions.explanation_english: Compulsory Retirement Compulsory Retirement is a major penalty under Rule 11(vii). Under statutory rules, no major penalty can ever be imposed on a government servant if proceedings were conducted purely under Rule 16 without holding a formal oral inquiry following the detailed sub-rules of Rule 14.

options_hindi: कर्मचारी के अनुरोध पर हर स्थिति में पूर्ण मौखिक जाँच कराना अनिवार्य है।
ज्ञापन को स्वतः नियम 14 के औपचारिक आरोप-पत्र में बदलना अनिवार्य है।
कारण दर्ज करके अनुरोध अस्वीकार कर सकता है और अभिलेखों के आधार पर निर्णय ले सकता है।

questions.question_english: A TGT is served a Rule 16 memorandum for negligence. He submits a representation denying the charges completely and demands an oral inquiry to prove his innocence. What is the Disciplinary Authority’s power in this situation?
options_english: The DA is legally bound to conduct a full oral inquiry whenever the employee requests it.
The DA must automatically convert the memorandum into a formal Rule 14 charge sheet.
The DA may reject the request recording reasons and decide based on records.
The DA must drop all charges immediately upon receiving a written denial statement.
questions.explanation_english: The DA may reject the request recording reasons and decide based on records. In minor penalty proceedings under Rule 16, holding an oral inquiry upon the employee’s request is not mandatory. The Disciplinary Authority has discretion to decide whether an inquiry is necessary; if it considers an inquiry unnecessary, it may reject the request by recording written reasons and decide based on records.

questions.question_english: During a Rule 14 inquiry, the charged officer has the fundamental right to:
options_english: Remain completely silent during hearings and force the IO to drop all articles of charge.
Demand the immediate administrative transfer of the designated Disciplinary Authority.
Unilaterally dictate the entire hearing schedule, location, and venue of the inquiry.
Cross-examine witnesses produced on behalf of the Disciplinary Authority.
questions.explanation_english: Cross-examine witnesses produced on behalf of the Disciplinary Authority. In a Rule 14 departmental inquiry, cross- examination of prosecution witnesses is a fundamental right of the charged government servant. It allows the employee to test the veracity, accuracy, and credibility of statements made by witnesses produced on behalf of the Disciplinary Authority to establish defense.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। नियम 14 की विभागीय जाँच में आरोपित सरकारी कर्मचारी को अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी की ओर से प्रस्तुत गवाहों से जिरह करने का अधिकार होता है। जिरह के माध्यम से कर्मचारी गवाहों के बयानों की विश्वसनीयता, सटीकता और सुसंगति की जाँच कर सकता है तथा अपने बचाव के लिए प्रश्न उठा सकता है।

questions.question_hindi: आरोपित अधिकारी जाँच अधिकारी से सरकारी अभिरक्षा में मौजूद एक विशेष दस्तावेज़ मँगवाने का अनुरोध करता है और कहता है कि वह उसके बचाव के लिए आवश्यक है। दस्तावेज़ रखने वाला विभागाध्यक्ष सार्वजनिक हित के विरुद्ध होने का दावा करते हुए विशेषाधिकार (privilege) जताता है। नियमों के अनुसार सही स्थिति क्या है?
options_hindi: यदि सार्वजनिक हित के आधार पर विशेषाधिकार का दावा किया जाता है, तो दस्तावेज़ मँगाने की माँग लागू नहीं की जाती।
जाँच अधिकारी को विभागाध्यक्ष से दस्तावेज़ निकलवाने की असीमित वैधानिक शक्ति है।
दस्तावेज़ न मिलने पर आरोपित अधिकारी का बचाव स्वतः सिद्ध माना जाएगा।

questions.question_english: A charged officer requests the Inquiry Officer to summon a specific document from government custody, claiming it is vital for their defense. The head of the department holding the document claims privilege, stating its production is against the public interest. What is the correct position under the rules?
options_english: If privilege is claimed in public interest, requisition is not enforced.
The IO holds statutory power to force the head of department to produce the document.
The charged officer’s defense is automatically deemed proved due to non-production.
The inquiry must be suspended indefinitely until a civil court orders its production.
questions.explanation_english: If privilege is claimed in public interest, requisition is not enforced. Under Rule 14(13), when an officer requisitions official documents for defense, the authority holding the document may claim privilege if producing it is contrary to public interest or state security. If privilege is formally claimed in writing, the Inquiry Officer cannot enforce requisition of that document.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। नियम 14(13) के अंतर्गत बचाव के लिए सरकारी दस्तावेज़ माँगे जाने पर, दस्तावेज़ रखने वाला प्राधिकारी यह दावा कर सकता है कि उसे प्रस्तुत करना सार्वजनिक हित या राज्य की सुरक्षा के प्रतिकूल होगा। यदि ऐसा विशेषाधिकार विधिवत दावा किया गया है, तो जाँच अधिकारी दस्तावेज़ प्रस्तुत कराने की माँग लागू नहीं कर सकता।

questions.question_hindi: आरोपित अधिकारी जाँच में बचाव पक्ष का एक गवाह लाता है। जाँच अधिकारी मौखिक रूप से यह कहकर गवाह का बयान दर्ज करने से इनकार करता है कि उसे पहले से पता है कि गवाह क्या कहेगा और उसका बयान अप्रासंगिक है। क्या यह कदम नियमों के अनुरूप है?
options_hindi: हाँ, जाँच अधिकारी बिना कारण दर्ज किए किसी भी गवाह को अस्वीकार करने का पूर्ण विवेकाधिकार रखता है।
नहीं, यदि जाँच अधिकारी किसी गवाह को बुलाने से इनकार करता है, तो उसे कारण लिखित रूप में दर्ज करने होंगे।
हाँ, बचाव पक्ष के गवाह केवल आपराधिक अदालतों में स्वीकार्य हैं, विभागीय जाँच में नहीं।
नहीं, जाँच अधिकारी को प्रासंगिकता की परवाह किए बिना हर प्रस्तुत व्यक्ति की जाँच करनी ही होगी।
questions.question_english: A charged officer brings a defense witness to the inquiry. The Inquiry Officer refuses to record the witness’s statement, verbally claiming, “I already know what he will say, it is irrelevant.” Is this action legally sustainable?
options_english: Yes, the IO holds absolute administrative discretion to refuse any witness without recording reasons.
No, if the IO refuses a witness, reasons must be recorded in writing.
Yes, defense witnesses are legally permissible only in criminal court trials, not inquiries.
No, the IO is legally required to examine every person presented, regardless of relevance.
questions.explanation_english: No, if the IO refuses a witness, reasons must be recorded in writing. The Inquiry Officer cannot disallow a defense witness arbitrarily or verbally. If the IO considers a witness irrelevant or immaterial to the charges, the IO has authority to refuse calling that witness, but must record explicit written reasons in the daily order sheet for such refusal.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। जाँच अधिकारी बचाव पक्ष के गवाह को मनमाने ढंग से या केवल मौखिक टिप्पणी करके अस्वीकार नहीं कर सकता। यदि वह गवाह को अप्रासंगिक या आरोपों से असंबद्ध मानता है, तो उसे गवाह न बुलाने के कारण लिखित रूप में दर्ज करने चाहिए। इससे जाँच की प्रक्रिया पारदर्शी रहती है और निर्णय की समीक्षा संभव होती है।

questions.question_english: Before the close of the case on behalf of the Disciplinary Authority, if the charged officer has not examined themselves as a witness, what must the Inquiry Officer generally do according to Rule 14(18)?

Immediately terminate the inquiry proceedings and hold all articles of charge proved.

Rule 14(18) requires the Inquiry Officer, before closing the Disciplinary Authority’s case, to question the charged officer about circumstances appearing in the evidence against them when the officer has not examined themselves as a witness.
